The varying widths of the 90% confidence intervals directly reflect the increasing uncertainty associated with longer time horizons. These might include sudden and unexpected economic shifts, such as a sharp recession or an unexpected boom, which could drastically alter the underlying conditions. Major geopolitical events, significant regulatory changes, or unforeseen technological disruptions could also introduce substantial volatility. Furthermore, any significant unexpected news directly relevant to the subject of the forecast—like a major company announcement, a new scientific discovery, or an impactful natural disaster—could quickly move the actual outcome beyond the boundaries I've outlined.
